cities.name: Agra
cities.overview: Agra, on the Yamuna, was the capital of the Mughal Empire for much of the 16th and 17th centuries. It holds three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and nearby Fatehpur Sikri.
cities.history: Sikandar Lodi made Agra his capital in the early 16th century, and it became one of the great Mughal cities under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan. Mughal emperors built Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal here.

cities.name: Fatehpur Sikri
cities.overview: A town 37 km west of Agra built around Emperor Akbar's short-lived red sandstone capital.

cities.name: Varanasi
cities.overview: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, Varanasi (Kashi or Banaras) is Hinduism's holiest city. Life, prayer and cremation all take place on its 80-odd ghats along the Ganga.
cities.history: One of the oldest continuously lived-in cities in the world, on the Ganges, and for long a centre of Hindu learning. Most of the ghats and temples seen today were rebuilt from the 18th century on by Maratha and other patrons.

cities.name: Lucknow
cities.overview: The capital of Uttar Pradesh was once the seat of the Nawabs of Awadh. It is known for its imambaras, refined Urdu culture, chikankari embroidery and kebabs.
cities.history: The capital of the Nawabs of Awadh from the 18th century, under whom it became a centre of music, poetry and cooking. It was the site of a long siege during the Revolt of 1857.

cities.name: Lakhimpur Kheri
cities.overview: A district in the Terai along the Nepal border, home to Dudhwa National Park.

cities.name: Prayagraj
cities.overview: Allahabad, the city at the confluence of the Ganges and Yamuna, host of the Kumbh Mela and home of the Nehru family.
cities.history: Called Prayag in old Hindu texts, it was renamed Allahabad by Akbar, who built a fort here in 1583. Its colleges and courts made it a centre of the independence movement.

cities.name: Mathura
cities.overview: An ancient city on the Yamuna, the Hindu birthplace of Krishna, 162 km from Delhi.

cities.name: Vrindavan
cities.overview: A temple town 15 km from Mathura, where Krishna is said to have spent his childhood.

cities.name: Ayodhya
cities.overview: A city on the Sarayu River, held to be the birthplace of Rama, now home to a major new temple.

cities.name: Jhansi
cities.overview: A Bundelkhand city that's forever linked to Rani Lakshmibai and the Revolt of 1857, and the rail gateway to Orchha.

cities.name: Gorakhpur
cities.overview: A city on the Rapti River in eastern Uttar Pradesh, the base for Kushinagar and the Buddhist circuit.

cities.name: Mirzapur
cities.overview: A Ganges town south of Varanasi, known for its carpets and the old fort at Chunar.

cities.name: Bahraich
cities.overview: A Terai district on the Nepal border, known for the forests of Katarniaghat.

cities.name: Pilibhit
cities.overview: A Terai town on the Nepal border, known for its tiger reserve.

cities.name: Banda
cities.overview: A Bundelkhand town, the base for the great hill fort at Kalinjar and for the pilgrim town of Chitrakoot.

places.name: Taj Mahal
places.shortDescription: The white marble mausoleum built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal, and one of the most recognised buildings on earth.
places.description: The Taj Mahal stands at the end of a formal Mughal garden on the bank of the Yamuna. Its white Makrana marble changes colour through the day, from pink at dawn to gold at sunset. Look closely to see the pietra dura inlay of semi-precious stones and the calligraphy that frames the arches. The mosque and guest house on either side are built in red sandstone, and Mehtab Bagh across the river offers a quieter sunset view.
places.history: Emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the tomb after the death of his wife Mumtaz Mahal in 1631. Around 20,000 artisans worked on it, and the main complex was completed by about 1653. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. Visit at sunrise for soft light and fewer people.

entryFee.note: ₹200 extra to enter the main mausoleum. Children under 15 free. Online tickets are slightly cheaper.

timings.hours: 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes before sunset

location.address: Dharmapuri, Forest Colony, Tajganj, Agra, Uttar Pradesh 282001

highlights: Sunrise view of the main dome

places.name: Agra Fort
places.shortDescription: The red sandstone fortress-palace of the Mughal emperors, with views across the Yamuna to the Taj Mahal.
places.description: Agra Fort's 2.5 km of walls enclose palaces, audience halls and mosques. Highlights include the Jahangiri Mahal, the white marble Khas Mahal and the Musamman Burj, an octagonal tower with a clear view of the Taj Mahal. Only part of the fort is open to the public; the rest is still used by the Indian Army.
places.history: Emperor Akbar rebuilt an older fort in red sandstone from 1565. His grandson Shah Jahan added marble palaces, and he spent his last years held captive here by his son Aurangzeb, looking out at the tomb he had built for his wife. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

entryFee.note: Children under 15 free. Online tickets are slightly cheaper.

places.name: Fatehpur Sikri
places.shortDescription: Emperor Akbar's red sandstone capital, abandoned within a few decades and preserved almost intact.
places.description: Fatehpur Sikri has two parts: the royal palaces, including the Diwan-i-Khas with its carved central pillar and the five-storey Panch Mahal, and the Jama Masjid, entered through the 54-metre Buland Darwaza. Inside the mosque courtyard is the white marble tomb of the Sufi saint Salim Chishti, where visitors tie threads on the screens to make a wish.
places.history: Akbar built the city between 1571 and 1585 to honour Salim Chishti, who had foretold the birth of his son. It served as the Mughal capital for about 14 years before being largely abandoned. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

entryFee.note: For the palace complex. The Jama Masjid and Salim Chishti's tomb are free.

location.address: Fatehpur Sikri, Agra district, Uttar Pradesh 283110

places.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
places.shortDescription: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva and the spiritual heart of Varanasi.
places.description: The temple's gold-plated spire rises above the old city near the Ganga. The Kashi Vishwanath Dham corridor, opened in 2021, now links the temple directly to the riverbank ghats with wide courtyards. Expect queues and security checks; phones, bags and cameras must be left in lockers. Early-morning mangala aarti requires advance booking.
places.history: A temple to Vishwanath has stood here for many centuries and was destroyed and rebuilt several times. The present temple was built in 1780 by Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore, and Maharaja Ranjit Singh later donated gold for its spire.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. Mahashivratri and the month of Shravan are especially crowded.

entryFee.note: Free darshan; paid options for faster entry and aarti.

timings.hours: About 3:00 AM – 11:00 PM, with breaks for aarti

location.address: Lahori Tola, Domari, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh 221001

places.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
places.shortDescription: Varanasi's busiest ghat, where the grand Ganga Aarti is performed every evening.
places.description: Each evening at sunset, young priests perform the Ganga Aarti here with large brass lamps, conch shells and chanting, watched by crowds on the steps and from boats on the river. In the morning the ghat fills with bathers and pilgrims. A dawn boat ride from here along the ghats to Manikarnika, the main cremation ghat, is the classic way to see Varanasi.
places.history: According to legend, Lord Brahma performed a ten-horse (dashashwamedha) sacrifice here to welcome Lord Shiva.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. Dev Deepawali, in November, lights up every ghat with lamps.

timings.hours: Open all day; Ganga Aarti at sunset (about 6:00–7:00 PM)

location.address: Dashashwamedh Ghat Rd, Ghats of Varanasi, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh 221001

places.name: Sarnath
places.shortDescription: The deer park where the Buddha gave his first sermon, with the Dhamek Stupa and the original Lion Capital of Ashoka.
places.description: Sarnath, 10 km from Varanasi, is one of the four main Buddhist pilgrimage sites. Walk among monastery ruins to the 34-metre Dhamek Stupa, visit temples built by Buddhist countries, and see the Lion Capital of Ashoka (India's national emblem) in the Sarnath Archaeological Museum.
places.history: After his enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, the Buddha came here around 528 BCE and preached his first sermon to five disciples. Emperor Ashoka built stupas and a pillar here in the 3rd century BCE, and the site flourished for over a thousand years.

entryFee.note: Small fees for the excavated site and the museum. The museum is closed on Fridays.

highlights: Lion Capital of Ashoka at the museum

places.name: Bara Imambara
places.shortDescription: A grand Nawabi complex with one of the world's largest vaulted halls and the Bhool Bhulaiya labyrinth.
places.description: The central hall of the Bara Imambara is about 50 metres long and built without beams or pillars to hold up the roof. Above it is the Bhool Bhulaiya, a maze of over a thousand narrow passages leading to rooftop views. The complex also includes the Asfi Mosque and a stepwell. Hire an authorised guide for the maze.
places.history: Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula built it in 1784 as a famine-relief project, giving work to thousands of people during a severe drought.

entryFee.note: Ticket includes the Bhool Bhulaiya and nearby monuments. Check rates at the gate.

timings.closedOn: Closed during prayer times on some days

places.name: Dudhwa National Park
places.shortDescription: Terai grasslands and sal forest on the Nepal border with tigers, swamp deer and rhinos.
places.description: Dudhwa is one of the few places where you can see tigers, leopards, one-horned rhinos and large herds of swamp deer (barasingha) in the same park. Explore its grasslands, wetlands and sal forest on jeep or elephant safaris. It is far less crowded than India's better-known tiger reserves and is a rewarding place for birdwatching.
places.history: Declared a national park in 1977 and part of a tiger reserve since 1987. One-horned rhinos were reintroduced here from Assam and Nepal in 1984.
places.bestTimeNote: The park is usually open from 15 November to 15 June.

entryFee.note: Entry, vehicle and guide fees apply. Book safaris through the UP forest department.

location.address: Dudhwa, Palia Kalan, Lakhimpur Kheri district, Uttar Pradesh 262902

places.name: Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah
places.shortDescription: The Baby Taj: an exquisite white marble tomb on the Yamuna, built before the Taj Mahal.
places.description: Small enough to take in at one glance, covered entirely in inlaid stone flowers and lattice. Many think it marks the move from red sandstone to white marble in Mughal building.
places.history: Built between 1622 and 1628, by the empress Nur Jahan for her father, Mirza Ghiyas Beg.

places.name: Mehtab Bagh
places.shortDescription: A Mughal garden across the Yamuna from the Taj Mahal, the best place to see it at sunset.
places.description: A square garden on the far river bank, lined up exactly with the Taj. There's little to see in the garden itself, but the view of the Taj at sunset is hard to beat.
places.history: It lies north of the Taj Mahal complex, on the flood plain of the Yamuna.

places.name: Akbar's Tomb, Sikandra
places.shortDescription: The mausoleum of the emperor Akbar in Sikandra, a huge sandstone tomb in a 119-acre garden.
places.description: A great gateway with white marble minarets leads to a five-storey tomb, unlike any other Mughal mausoleum. Deer roam the grounds.
places.history: Built in 1605 to 1613 by Akbar's son, Jahangir.

places.name: Sur Sarovar Bird Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A lake and bird sanctuary off the Agra to Delhi highway, with a sloth bear rescue centre.
places.description: A wide lake with waterbirds off the highway, popular in winter. The Agra Bear Rescue Facility looks after sloth bears once used as dancing bears.

places.name: Krishna Janmasthan
places.shortDescription: The temple complex in Mathura at the traditional birthplace of Krishna.
places.description: Security is tight in this large complex, and phones can't be taken in. Pilgrims visit the small prison-like cell that marks the birthplace itself, and the crowds peak at Janmashtami.

places.name: Banke Bihari Temple
places.shortDescription: The most popular temple in Vrindavan, known for its curtain drawn repeatedly over the deity.
places.description: A crowded and joyful temple. A curtain is drawn across the deity every few minutes, and there's no ringing of bells, so as not to disturb the child-god.

places.name: Prem Mandir
places.shortDescription: A huge white marble temple on the edge of Vrindavan, with a colour-changing light show at night.
places.description: Set in a 22-hectare garden with life-size scenes from Krishna's life. It's most striking at dusk, as coloured lights play across the marble.
places.history: Founded by Kripalu Maharaj and opened in 2012.

places.name: Assi Ghat
places.shortDescription: The southernmost ghat of Varanasi, with its popular Subah-e-Banaras morning music and aarti.
places.description: Long-stay students and travellers gather here, and it's a good place to begin a boat ride. Mornings start with music, yoga and an aarti in the Subah-e-Banaras programme.

places.name: Manikarnika Ghat
places.shortDescription: The main cremation ghat of Varanasi, where fires have burned for centuries.
places.description: Fires burn around the clock, and it's considered one of the most sacred places to be cremated for Hindus. Be respectful, and don't take pictures.
places.history: One of the oldest and most sacred ghats on the Ganges in Varanasi.

places.name: Ramnagar Fort
places.shortDescription: An 18th-century sandstone fort on the east bank of the Ganges, home of the Maharaja of Benares.
places.description: A red fort that's still partly lived in, facing Tulsi Ghat across the river. Its museum shows old cars, palanquins and arms, and the Ramlila here is famous.
places.history: Built in 1750 by the ruler of Banaras State.

places.name: Chunar Fort
places.shortDescription: A riverside fort held by many rulers in turn, 34 km from Mirzapur, on a rock above the Ganges.
places.description: A long fort on a rock high above a bend in the Ganges. Afghans, Mughals and the British all fought for it, and it's rarely visited now.
places.history: Sher Shah Suri, Humayun and Akbar all held it in turn.

places.name: Rumi Darwaza
places.shortDescription: A 60-foot gateway built by Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula in 1784, the symbol of Lucknow.
places.description: A huge, flower-topped arch standing on the road through old Lucknow. It's sometimes called the Turkish Gate.
places.history: Built in 1784 and modelled, it's said, on the Sublime Porte in Istanbul.

places.name: Chota Imambara
places.shortDescription: The Palace of Lights, a Shia hall in Lucknow, with chandeliers and gilded walls.
places.description: A white, gold-domed building with mirrors and Belgian chandeliers inside, and walls covered in Arabic calligraphy. A tank and fine smaller tombs stand in the garden.
places.history: Built as a congregation hall for Shia Muslims by Muhammad Ali Shah of Awadh, in the 1830s.

places.name: The Residency, Lucknow
places.shortDescription: The ruins of the British Residency, scene of a long siege during the Revolt of 1857.
places.description: Roofless, bullet-marked buildings in a calm garden, with a cemetery and a small museum. It's been left in much the state it was after the siege.
places.history: The home of the British Resident General at the court of the Nawab. It was under siege for months during the 1857 Revolt.

places.name: Ram Mandir
places.shortDescription: The major Hindu temple in Ayodhya, consecrated in 2024, at the traditional birthplace of Rama.
places.description: A large temple in pink sandstone, now one of the most visited in India. Expect a long wait and tight security: phones and bags need to be left outside.
places.history: Consecrated in January 2024, after a long dispute over the site that ended with a Supreme Court ruling in 2019.

places.name: Hanuman Garhi
places.shortDescription: A hilltop Hanuman temple in Ayodhya, reached by 76 steps, and one of the city's most important.
places.description: A busy fortress-like temple that's traditionally visited before going to the Ram temple, with a good view from the top.

places.name: Triveni Sangam
places.shortDescription: The sacred meeting of the Ganges, Yamuna and mythical Saraswati, site of the great Kumbh Mela.
places.description: Boats take pilgrims to the point where the Ganges and Yamuna visibly meet, with brown water against green. It's the holiest bathing place on the Kumbh circuit.
places.bestTimeNote: The Kumbh Mela returns to Prayagraj every 12 years; a smaller Magh Mela is held each January.

places.name: Allahabad Fort
places.shortDescription: A huge fort built by Akbar in 1583 on the banks of the Yamuna, near the Sangam.
places.description: Largely in army hands, so you can see only a part of it, but the Patalpuri temple and Akshayavat tree inside are open to pilgrims. An Ashokan pillar stands inside as well.
places.history: Built by the emperor Akbar in 1583, and now protected as a monument of national importance.

places.name: Anand Bhavan
places.shortDescription: The historic home of the Nehru family in Prayagraj, now a museum of the independence movement.
places.description: A big, veranda-lined house where the Nehrus lived and where leaders of the freedom struggle met. The rooms are kept as they were.
places.history: Bought by Motilal Nehru in the 1930s, after the family's first home, Swaraj Bhavan, was given to the Congress Party.

places.name: Jhansi Fort
places.shortDescription: A hilltop fort on Bangira, famous as the stronghold of Rani Lakshmibai in 1857.
places.description: A big granite fort above the town, with cannons and a Shiva temple. Guides show the spot from which the Rani is said to have leapt on her horse to escape.
places.history: Besieged by the British in 1858, and the place from which Rani Lakshmibai made her escape.

places.name: Kalinjar Fort
places.shortDescription: A vast Chandela stronghold on an isolated hill, one of India's largest fortified cities.
places.description: A long plateau-top fort, with temples, huge rock-cut figures and old water tanks. Mahmud of Ghazni and Sher Shah Suri both fought here.
places.history: One of eight great forts built by the Chandela emperors, and their military capital.

places.name: Chitrakoot Dham
places.shortDescription: A holy town on the Mandakini River, where Rama is said to have spent part of his exile.
places.description: Pilgrims bathe at Ramghat and walk around sacred Kamadgiri hill. The town straddles the Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh border.

places.name: Kushinagar
places.shortDescription: The town where the Buddha is believed to have died, a major Buddhist pilgrimage site.
places.description: A green, peaceful site with temples built by Buddhists from many countries. Its Mahaparinirvana Temple has a 6 m reclining Buddha that's over 1,500 years old.

places.name: Gorakhnath Math
places.shortDescription: The large temple complex of the Nath order in Gorakhpur, with a flame said to be always burning.
places.description: A big, active temple centre named after the medieval saint Gorakshanath. The Makar Sankranti fair each January is its largest event.

places.name: Shravasti
places.shortDescription: The capital of the old Kosala kingdom, where the Buddha lived most after his enlightenment.
places.description: Quiet excavated monasteries and stupas at Saheth-Maheth, near the Rapti River. A Buddhist circuit stop with few visitors.

images.credit: Varun Shiv Kapur from New Delhi, India

places.name: Katarniaghat Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A Terai forest of 400 sq km on the Nepal border, known for its gharials and river dolphins.
places.description: Sal forest and grassland along the Girwa River, where boat trips can bring you close to gharials and Gangetic dolphins. It's also part of the Dudhwa Tiger Reserve.

places.name: Pilibhit Tiger Reserve
places.shortDescription: A Terai tiger reserve on the Nepal border, known for high tiger numbers in tall grass and sal.
places.description: Dense sal forest and tall grass along the Sharda River and its canals. Tiger numbers have grown so well here that it won an international award.
places.history: Notified as a tiger reserve in 2014.
